productionBuild.warning: Vite reports the main JS entry is larger than 500 kB; initial total remains under the 10 MB gate.

visualChanges: Added manual pause, frozen simulation, explicit resume, and clean restart from the pause card.
Hiding the document now freezes the expedition and releases touch input; returning resumes it without a delta-time jump.
Added a production-generated service worker that precaches the app shell, all bundled JS/CSS chunks, manifest, and original icons.
Added 192×192 and 512×512 PWA icons; production browser QA confirms a cold offline navigation and expedition start.
Touch controls are measured fully inside 844×390, 800×360, and 915×412 landscape viewports.

qualitativeComparison.sameSeedAgainstIteration05: At all tested landscape widths, the main cell and final-gate scene remain visible; the joystick stays bottom-left, action controls bottom-right, and threat cue at top-right. The pause card is centered and offers both resume and restart without obscuring the underlying game state.
qualitativeComparison.userReference: The original scientific-microscope palette and translucent procedural organisms remain consistent with the supplied still. No original executable was supplied, so the comparison remains visual/qualitative and makes no gameplay-superiority claim.
qualitativeComparison.assetProvenance: 3D organisms/world geometry and the PWA icon are original project assets; no Spore/EA logos or game assets are used.

limitations: QA used touch-capable headless Chromium with software rendering at scale 1; no physical Android device or actual home-screen install action was performed.
The PWA manifest/icon, service-worker cache, and cold offline start were tested locally at the build root; no GitHub Pages deployment under a nested URL has been exercised.
The 60 FPS target and automatic stable 30 FPS quality fallback remain unmeasured/unimplemented for constrained Android devices.
The 6.761 MB minified Babylon entry continues to trigger Vite’s >500 kB chunk warning; total dist is 7,346,864 bytes.

Automated expedition E2E uses QA hooks to accelerate biomass milestones and final travel; touch steering, resource pickup, action controls, pause, pointer cancellation, visibility transitions, and end states are separately exercised.
